races.title: State Assembly, District 55
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Isaac G. Bryan
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly, first elected in a 2021 special election for District 54 and now representing District 55. Holds a UCLA master's degree in public policy analysis. Former senior advisor to Sydney Kamlager and founding director of the UCLA Black Policy Project.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, California Environmental Voters, Sierra Club Angeles Chapter and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Isaac Bryan was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found no record of his positions or actions on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored was empty on the page we read, so we could not confirm any specific bill. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys. His 2022 survey answers were general and did not address these topics. The Measure J campaign role comes from his own survey answer, not independent reporting. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the material available.

qual.background: Assembly member since 2021, after working as an advisor to state and local elected officials, including as Senior Advisor to Sydney Kamlager. He holds a UCLA master's in public policy analysis and founded the UCLA Black Policy Project.
qual.why: Several years of legislative service plus a policy and advisory career fit the law-and-budget job. The score gives no credit for his committee chair.

cands.name: Ashley M. Brown
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California State Assembly District 55 in 2026. She advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary to the November general election against incumbent Isaac Bryan (D). Her jobs and any prior offices are not documented in the sources reviewed.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as receiving a voter guide recommendation from Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide (Sway voting group).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Ashley Brown was born or raised, when she came to California, or her work history and any offices she has held. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and no other source gave her stated positions. We found no documented actions, public statements on data centers or development, or controversies. The only page available was a short Ballotpedia profile, which gives no biographical detail.
